decisions.reason: The question covers real-world pedestrian–robot interactions but omits how data collected by a moving robot can support pedestrian perception and motion prediction for social navigation.

The method gives the indoor and outdoor settings, two 3D LiDARs, five cameras, and 360-degree camera coverage. It omits manual operation, crowded locations in Seoul, and pulse-per-second synchronization.
The method gives 20-second sequences at 10 Hz. It omits the 60 scenes, 60K images, 12K point-cloud frames, 2D and 3D box annotations, object IDs, and multilayer semantic maps.
The poster does not describe robot ego-motion compensation or state that training, validation, and test subsets contain different scenes.

The finding names all three comparison datasets and reports that SiT has more instances satisfying both conditions. The finding and caption define those conditions as sharing the same semantic space and being within 2 meters.
The poster omits the 3D detection and tracking baselines, the center-distance thresholds used for detection mAP, and the tracking metrics.
The poster omits the forecasting history and horizon, the candidate counts and displacement metrics, the three baselines, and the reported error reductions from semantic maps.
The poster omits the raw-sensor benchmark, its 7-second prediction horizon and outputs, the model variants, and the four evaluation measures.
The poster omits the authors’ statement that time constraints prevented collection at the scale of hundreds of thousands of frames.

notes: AI review based on the supplied export, editable text, and frozen checklist. The title and section headings establish a clear path from question and method to finding and figure.
